Data Encryption Standard

Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. 'Laptop encryption' renamed to 'Device encryption' to reflect coverage of tablets as well as laptops — no requirement changed for laptops specifically.

Purpose and scope

This standard sets out how Alderbridge encrypts data held on a laptop or tablet. It applies to every Alderbridge-issued laptop and, newly reflected in this version's title, every issued tablet.

Policy statement

All Alderbridge laptops, and as before any issued tablet, use full-disk encryption enabled by IT before issue, protecting resident and staff data if a device is lost or stolen.

Definitions

**Full-disk encryption** encryption applied to an entire device's storage, so data cannot be read without the correct credentials, even if the physical storage is removed. **Device** covers both a laptop and an issued tablet under this version's renamed title; the underlying laptop requirement is unchanged from the previous version. **Enabled before issue** the requirement that encryption is confirmed active before a device reaches its user, never enabled retrospectively after use has begun.

Enable full-disk encryption on every laptop and issued tablet before it is issued to a staff member.

Verify encryption status as part of IT's pre-issue checklist, never issuing a device where this check has not passed.

Report a device suspected to have been issued without encryption enabled to IT immediately for urgent remediation.

Include encryption verification for both laptops and tablets in the annual device audit across all sites.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This standard works alongside the Mobile Device Management Policy (governing the wider device management framework encryption sits within) and the Cyber Incident Response Plan (relevant where a lost device's encryption status affects the incident response).

Report a suspected cyber incident to IT immediately.

IT classifies the incident against the four-tier severity model within 30 minutes.

IT isolates the affected device or system from the network immediately, regardless of severity tier.

IT notifies Alderbridge's cyber insurance provider within 24 hours of a Tier 3 or above classification; this is a new mandatory step introduced in this version, previously left to case-by-case judgement.

Do not pay a ransomware demand, and do not negotiate with an attacker; a Tier 4 ransomware-related decision now requires Board Chair co-approval alongside the Chief Executive, a new safeguard introduced in this version.

The Data Protection Officer assesses within 12 hours whether the incident constitutes a personal data breach requiring ICO notification within 72 hours.

Restore affected systems from a verified clean backup only once IT confirms the original vulnerability has been addressed.

Contact the regional IT emergency contact for out-of-hours support at a Tier 2 or higher incident.

Severity classification table

Tier	Description	Example	Response
Tier 1	Single device, no evidence of spread	One laptop displaying a suspicious prompt	IT service desk handles directly during normal hours
Tier 2	Single site affected, contained locally	A site's local network shows unusual traffic	IT escalates to the on-call IT lead; regional emergency contact engaged if out of hours
Tier 3	Multiple sites or a core system affected	A shared care records system shows signs of compromise	IT Director engaged; Business Continuity Plan considered; cyber insurance provider notified
Tier 4	Organisation-wide, or resident safety directly implicated	Ransomware affecting the medication administration system network-wide	Chief Executive and Board Chair engaged immediately; Business Continuity Plan activated; cyber insurance provider notified

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where an affected system is critical to immediate resident safety regardless of its formal severity tier, IT prioritises a safe manual fallback process alongside containment, treating the resident-safety implication as at least Tier 3, which also now triggers the cyber insurance notification step.

Self-neglect** a resident's own inability or unwillingness to care for themselves or their environment to a degree that risks their health or safety, now explicitly recognised within this suite. **Multi-agency information sharing** the principles governing what safeguarding information Alderbridge shares with an external agency such as the local authority or police.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** reports a safeguarding concern immediately, including a self-neglect concern, following the specific procedure relevant to the type of concern. **The registered manager** leads the response to most safeguarding concerns. **The site Safeguarding Champion**, referred to consistently by this title throughout this version, provides local expertise and support. **The organisation-level Safeguarding Lead** oversees the suite and coordinates multi-agency information sharing per the new appendix.

Refer to the Adult Safeguarding Policy for the general framework and reporting route for any safeguarding concern.

Refer to the Allegations Against Staff Procedure where the concern involves a member of staff's own conduct.

Refer to the Missing Person Procedure where a resident cannot be located.

Refer to Body Mapping Guidance for how to document an unexplained mark or injury.

Refer to the Resident Finances and Appointeeship Policy for a financial concern, escalated to the organisation-level Safeguarding Lead directly.

Refer to the new Self-Neglect Guidance where a resident's own care of themselves or their environment raises a concern; this is newly added to the suite in this version.

Share information with an external agency only in line with the multi-agency information sharing appendix below, balancing a resident's confidentiality against the safety benefit of appropriate disclosure.

Multi-agency information sharing appendix

Situation	Information sharing principle	Typical recipient
Ongoing safeguarding investigation	Share what is necessary and proportionate for the investigation	Local authority safeguarding team, police where relevant
LADO referral	Share full relevant conduct and employment context	Local Authority Designated Officer
Missing person	Share immediately, full description and last known information	Police
Routine multi-agency review meeting	Share a summary relevant to the meeting's purpose only	Attending agency representatives
